newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Short Australian bonds remain buyers option.
newsitem.headline: Short Australian bonds remain buyers option.

text.p: *Short Australian bonds yields were near to this year's lows as this part of the curve remained attractive following last week's official rate cut, and as few would discount another.
*Local focus on Friday's April retail trade data.
Short Australian bonds yields were near to this year's lows as this part of the curve remained attractive following last week's official rate cut.

With a spread of around 85 basis points to the cash rate at 5.50 basis points, analysts said there is still potential for this part of the curve to rally further, particular as few would discount another easing after last Friday's surprise move.
"The easing and growth bias by the RBA suggests that further easing this cycle cannot be completely ruled out," said Su-lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank Australia.
Today's shock 2.1 percent drop in first quarter business inventories, against a forecast 0.5 percent rise, was expected to detract 1.7 percent from GDP due next week.
This was much larger than the 0.3 percent that had been expected and added to thoughts of a further easing.

"Recent data suggest that there is still a stronger chance of disappoinment in growth than in inflation this year," said economists at Bankers Trust Australia. "Accordingly, although we still believe that growth will pick up over the course of 1997/98, if there were to be another move in interest rates this year it would clearly be downwards," they said.

While the short-end is finding support, longer dated stock remains vulnerable to moves offshore and particularly with the U.S. still wary that the Federal Reserve will tighten policy at the next policy meeting in July.
Traders feel that the yield spread tightening to the U.S. since last Friday's 50 basis point rate cut has gone as far as it can to around 75 basis points under the current climate.
However, the key focus for the market will be Friday's release of April retail trade as an update to current demand.
Forecasts centre on a slim 0.5 percent rise after the 0.3 percent fall in March.

The local market's firm tone saw it outpace the dollar bloc again. Canadian debt underperformed amid foreign selling on Wednesday, linked to the approach of next week's Canadian election. The Canadian market has recently been undermined by the threat of a Fed tightening.
The three-year bond contract finally broke 93.60, the high seen immediately after last week's rate cut, but stiff resistance is now at 93.65, the 1997 peak.
